slides.headline: October 9, 1949: India created an army of citizens who kept their day jobs.
C. Rajagopalachari formally launched India's Territorial Army
slides.body: As India's first Indian Governor-General, Rajagopalachari launched the Territorial Army under the Territorial Army Act of 1948 - a volunteer 'second line of defence' made up of ordinary citizens with regular civilian careers, who train for military service and can be mobilized in national emergencies.

slides.headline: 77 years later, it's still built on the same idea: a soldier who isn't a full-time soldier.
slides.body: October 9 is observed every year as Territorial Army Day. The force remains one of the few institutions where a civilian career and military readiness are meant to coexist, not compete.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat doesn't need every citizen in uniform - just enough who are willing to be.
slides.body: The Territorial Army's citizen-soldier model is a quiet reminder that national defence doesn't always require a standing army at full size - sometimes it requires a standing offer.
